rules.statement: Make a development convenience (developer keys, developer CORS, development seeds) register nothing unless its configuration section is present, rather than gating it on an environment check.
rules.why: A convenience that turns itself on in every non-Production host persists state, such as seeded clients, in hosts that never asked for it. Gating on configuration keeps it inert by default.
rules.check: Look for development-only registrations that check IHostEnvironment.IsDevelopment() or similar, or that register services when their configuration section is absent.

rules.statement: Decide the environment in exactly one production-safety check that refuses every development-only configuration section in Production and lists each offending section in a single report; don't add a second environment check elsewhere.
rules.why: When two places decide the environment, they can disagree about what Production refuses.
rules.check: Look for new environment checks in composition or registration code outside the single production-safety registration, and for development sections the Production check doesn't refuse.

rules.statement: Don't give library options collections host-specific defaults (origins, client ids, redirect URIs). Start them empty and have the host's environment overlay declare the entries.
rules.why: The configuration binder appends configured entries to a collection that already holds some, so configuration can extend such a default but never replace it.
rules.check: Look at options classes for collection properties initialized with concrete identifiers, URLs or client ids instead of an empty collection.

rules.statement: Don't let a development convenience create in-memory signing keys or intercept the tenant's key read. Every host signs with persisted keys read back through the production path.
rules.why: In-memory keys regenerate on restart, differ across replicas, invalidate tokens issued earlier, and make the runtime, the JWKS endpoint and the management API disagree about which keys exist.
rules.check: Look for development registrations that replace the key or tenant factory, or that generate keys in memory instead of provisioning them through the store.

rules.statement: Don't give a root key or key-protection provider setting a default or fallback. Validate at startup that it isn't blank, and have the lookup throw with the setting's name instead of choosing a provider.
rules.why: A fallback to an ephemeral provider starts a host with a root key that is lost on restart, which makes every stored secret unreadable, and outside Production this happens silently.
rules.check: Look for a default value for the key-protection provider, or for code that picks a provider when the setting is missing instead of failing with an error that names the setting.

rules.statement: Select an ephemeral (lost-on-restart) root key provider only explicitly, in development, conformance or test configuration, and have Production refuse both the ephemeral provider and an unset one.
rules.why: An ephemeral root key loses every stored secret on restart, so it must never be reached by accident or deployed.
rules.check: Look for the ephemeral provider being selected in production, staging or shared configuration or in chart defaults, and for Production checks that miss it or an unset provider.

rules.statement: Don't commit development credentials (bootstrap secrets, administrator passwords, root keys, private keys) in launch profiles or appsettings. Generate them once per machine and supply them through environment variables or user secrets.
rules.why: A committed development credential puts a secret in the repository, and a printed generated secret ends up in logs.
rules.check: Look in launchSettings.json, appsettings*.json and similar files for secret, password, key or PEM values, and look for code that logs generated secrets.

rules.statement: Validate each configured CORS allowed origin at startup as a browser Origin header value: an http or https scheme and a host with an optional port, with no user information, path, query, fragment or trailing slash. Fail with an error that names the offending configuration entry and its index.
rules.why: An entry that can never match a request is a silent misconfiguration, so it should stop the host with a clear error.
rules.check: Look for CORS origin options that are bound without a validator, or without ValidateOnStart, or whose errors don't name the configuration path.
